A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OS-Genesis and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–G. Corresponding content can be matched despite the appendix expansion and figure revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original GUI-agent evaluations on AndroidWorld, AndroidControl, and WebArena, together with reward-model ablations and data analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original evaluations and adds experiments comparing trajectory reward scores across models and against human annotations.

M1.justification: Reverse task synthesis, graded trajectory scoring, reward-proportional sampling, and the two training objectives remain unchanged. Appendix F tests Qwen2.5-VL-72B as an alternative scorer without reporting a revised algorithm or main training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain AndroidWorld, AndroidControl high- and low-level tasks, and WebArena. The new scoring-alignment studies sample mobile and web trajectories within existing coverage; they introduce no distinct GUI environment or execution scenario.

E2.justification: Figure 5 removes Task-Driven from the reward-strategy comparison, although it remains in the main benchmark tables. Appendix F adds comparisons between GPT-4o and Qwen2.5-VL-72B scoring and between TRM scores and human ratings. Main benchmark comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix F adds scoring-alignment protocols with stated samples of 200 web/mobile trajectories for model comparison and 100 for human comparison, using Spearman correlation. The allocation of these samples between domains is not explicit. Existing benchmark settings and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendices F.1–F.2 provide targeted checks of TRM consistency across model backbones and agreement with human judgments. Existing diversity, scaling, and human-data analyses remain, while the reward-strategy ablation figure is revised.

E5.justification: Tables 5–6 introduce Spearman correlations and associated p-values for the new scoring studies. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty for the main benchmark results, and v2 does not establish an increase in evaluation runs.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 are unchanged. New model-scoring correlations are 0.788 for web and 0.729 for mobile; human/TRM correlations are 0.798 and 0.813, respectively. Figure 5 also changes Qwen's AC-Type(L) ordering from w/o RM > TRM > Labeler to TRM > Labeler > w/o RM. Unlabeled radial scales prevent exact score comparisons.

T1.justification: The instruction mappings, Algorithm 1 sampling rule, and training losses in Equations 1–2 are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, proofs, or derivations are added; Spearman correlation is used as an evaluation statistic.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about interaction-driven synthesis, trajectory quality and diversity, and improved GUI-agent performance. The added validation does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix F newly interprets scoring agreement as supporting an open-source TRM alternative and alignment with human judgments. The added trajectory-construction limitation explicitly discusses model-constrained trajectory yield, closely related to the saturation explanation already present in Section 5.3.

D1.justification: Appendix F identifies the alternative scorer as Qwen2.5-VL-72B and specifies that human annotators use the existing TRM scoring guidelines. Annotator numbers and rating aggregation remain unspecified. Existing prompts, image-processing settings, hardware disclosures, and project access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Qwen2.5-VL technical report by Bai et al. (2025) for the new scorer experiment. The OS-ATLAS and black-box tuning references are updated versions of already cited works. The broader related-work positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 removes a duplicated introduction sentence, adds an Appendix F cross-reference and two subsections, and includes acknowledgments and author contributions. Author metadata and some bibliography entries also change. The main narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Figure 5 is redrawn with different colors, markers, grid, legend placement, and three rather than four series. Tables 5–6 are added, Figure 3 receives small text-layout adjustments, and Figure 9 moves without changing its content. The overall document layout is retained.

improvement.justification: The new human and cross-model agreement studies provide useful validation of TRM that v1 lacked, while preserving the main benchmark evidence. The gain is limited by unspecified annotation details and Figure 5's unexplained ordering change. Scoring correlation also does not establish equivalent downstream agent performance with the alternative scorer.
